mappings.note: asks for the definitional difference between an equation and an identity; no outcome defines 'identity' - LO-1 to LO-5 all assume it and go straight to proving, expanding or factorising - so the competency is the ceiling
the pattern is (n+1)^2 + (n-1)^2 - 2n^2 = 2, which is the (a+b)^2 and (a-b)^2 pair of LO-1 used to explain a numerical regularity; no factorising is asked
plain expansion by the (a+b)^2 identity of LO-1; the distractors differ only in the middle term, so that identity is exactly what is graded
(a+b+c)^2 is named in LO-4 and in no other outcome; the two-term squares of LO-1 do not reach three terms
factorises a quadratic and the check is against the perfect-square identity - LO-3's 'checks the result against the matching identity'; no tiles or area diagram, so not LO-2
104 x 96 as (100+4)(100-4) - the a^2 - b^2 identity of LO-1 applied to arithmetic rather than to symbols
splits 7x into 3x and 4x to reach (x+3)(x+4) - the middle-term method of LO-3; LO-4's (x+a)(x+b) is the expanding direction, this is the factorising one
cube of a binomial with a negative second term, which only LO-4 covers; the distractors test the 3a^2b and 3ab^2 coefficients
simplifies a rational algebraic expression by factorising numerator and denominator - the second clause of LO-5, word for word
the x^3+y^3+z^3-3xyz identity carries the item (LO-5), but xy+yz+zx first has to be recovered from (x+y+z)^2, which is LO-4
the assertion is the (a+b)^2 identity instantiated at (x+5)^2, so LO-1; the reason is the definition of an identity, which no outcome states
both clauses are the x^3+y^3+z^3-3xyz identity and its zero-sum consequence - LO-5's first clause, not the cube-of-a-binomial of LO-4
graded on spotting that 105 x 95 needs a^2 - b^2 and not (a+b)^2; both identities belong to LO-1, which is why the reason is false but the assertion true
the reason clause is the 'check against the matching identity' step of LO-3 stated in general, and the assertion is that check carried out on 4x^2-12x+9
both statements are forms of the cube of a binomial difference, which LO-4 names; the assertion's sign error on 3xy(x+y) is the discriminator
the (a+b)^2 identity expanded symbolically; paired with item 21 which uses (a-b)^2 numerically
105^2 split as (100+5)^2 - the (a+b)^2 identity turned on a number, the mental-arithmetic use of LO-1
middle-term splitting with both factors negative; LO-3, and distinguished from item 5 by not being a perfect square
three-term square with coefficients on two of the terms - LO-4's (a+b+c)^2 applied rather than merely recognised, as item 4 does
same (a+b+c)^2 identity as item 19, but with a negative middle term so the cross-term signs are the graded step
193^2 as (200-7)^2 - the (a-b)^2 member of LO-1, chosen over (a+b)^2 because the nearer round number is above
recognises a perfect-square trinomial and factorises it, which is LO-3's identity-check clause; see the defect note - the printed middle term 149h does not match the answer (79+h)^2, which needs 158h
middle-term splitting with a negative constant, so the two factors take opposite signs - still LO-3, and the hardest sign case of the three factorising items
difference of two cubes, which LO-4 names explicitly; LO-3 is restricted to quadratics so it cannot carry a cubic
sum of two cubes - the companion identity to item 24 within the same LO-4 clause, differing only in the sign of the middle term of the quadratic factor
